A special meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor McKeown at 5:30 p.m., on

  car. The City does not admit to the allegation in the lawsuit, but to avoid the
  expense and burden of further litigation, the City Attorney’s Office

  Ex parteCommunications

  Councilmember Davis, read a statement into the record: My husband works
  for Dell EMC, which is a subsidiary of Dell Technologies. Dell Technologies
  is a publicly traded corporation. My husband has never met Michael Bell,
  and is not an Officer, Director or Managing Agent for Dell Technologies or
  any subsidiary. He has no relationship with any person or entity that has any
  interest in the Miramar/Fairmont. His compensation will not be affected in
  any way by the Council’s decision on the Miramar. Nevertheless, on
  September 10, after Planning Commission approved the Miramar project and

  6
  September 29, 2020
   I knew it would be coming to Council, I asked for an opinion of the interim
  City Attorney as to whether I had a conflict of interest that would prohibit me
  from hearing or voting on the matter. Sometime later, I received inquiries
  from members of the public as to whether I would recuse myself. I told them
  I already had asked for an opinion of the Interim City Attorney and that I
  would abide by his decision. I spoke with the City Attorney about it on
  September 21. In that conversation, he opined there was no conflict, but he
  advised me to contact the Fair Political Practices Commission. I called the
  FPPC that same day but could not get through until Tuesday, September 22.
  The FPPC told me to send a request in writing, which I did. On September
  23, I received what the FPPC characterized as conservative, informal advice
  that I should recuse myself. Although I have asked for a formal opinion, I
  still have not received it. Therefore, on the basis of the informal opinion, I
  will be recusing myself from the hearing tonight. My decision on any future
  items that might relate to this project is subject to my getting a formal
  opinion from the FPPC.

Questions asked and answered of staff included: during the three-year
construction timeline, how will the city deal with the Transient Occupancy
Tax (TOT) loss; does the enhanced Transportation Demand Management
(TDM) requirement need to be added to the draft development agreement;
does the affordable housing component violate any of the current laws and
regulations; did the Environmental Impact Report (EIR) look at bluff stability
issues and air quality concerns; what processes are in place to ensure that
structural integrity is maintained in the surrounding neighborhoods and how
wide does that range go; why are there only 42 affordable housing units
being proposed; are the affordable housing units geared more for family
units; is the future gains in TOT payment really a benefit to the city, or is it
more of a benefit to the developer, since borrowing money is currently so
cheap right now; if there weren’t condominiums in the project, what amount
would go to affordable housing; has there been any discussion about
providing offsite transportation for construction workers as a part of traffic
mitigation; what would the TOT be if the condos were replaced with hotel
rooms; how are you going to keep workers from parking on the side streets,
when there aren’t enough parking spaces in the plan; what provisions could
be placed in the agreement to address minority hiring in the construction of
this project; how does the parking cash-out work; how does the city utilize
the $75,000 affordable lodging fee; where does the project go from here, if
the Council approves it; is there anything the city can do to make sure they
are receiving the fair value from property taxes, if the developer decides they
don’t want to go through with the development agreement entitlements; will
benefits employees are receiving when the construction starts, be retained by
them until the project is completed; will the developer have amenities for
public cyclist to park their bikes on the property; would a Landmarks
decision change the outside façade or reduce the room sizes; ways to mitigate
additional traffic on California Street; what was the designation for the four
impacted intersections before this project; does staff have an objection to
releasing the amount of number of condos that can be rented to increase the
TOT; are people required to buy food in order to have access to the elevated
